title: Miscellaneous Steganography and Artifact Analysis Quick Reference
description: Three basics: file headers, strings, and steganography
detail:
1. file + xxd header: changing the extension does not change the real format; repair png/jpg/zip/rar headers
2. strings | grep -iE 'flag|key|ctf'
3. binwalk -e: nested archives/embedded files
4. Images: zsteg (png/bmp LSB), stegsolve (frames/channels), exiftool (comments/GPS)
5. Archives: fake encryption (edit the hex flag), brute force (zip2john + hashcat -m 13600), known-plaintext attack (bkcrack)
6. Audio: WAV LSB (SilentEye/Audacity spectrogram)
7. Packet captures: filter http/ftp in Wireshark and export objects; scripts to reconstruct USB keyboard traffic
8. Forensics: memory (volatility3) process cmdline/filescan to search for sensitive artifacts; mount disk images and search
9. Encoding chains: base families/ROT/XOR/Dutch National Flag-like patterns by characteristics (CyberChef magic)
In assessment targets, miscellaneous artifacts are often hidden in files on the target host; do not ignore download directories.
commands: binwalk -e file.png && strings -n 6 file.png | grep -i flag
